messages.subject: problem with renderUI() and JavaScript
parts:
Hello!

I'm having some trouble with renderUI() and am hoping someone can help.  Basically, I want my Shiny app to produce a list of <li/> elements that are draggable (using Gridster.js).  It works perfectly when I had code each <li> into the ui part (see commented code below).  However, when I use renderUI() and uiOutput() to dynamically generate the <li> elements, the dragging functionality goes away.  Have I missed an important step?  Thank you very much!

To get the code below to work, you will need to download Gridster (http://gridster.net/#download) and put it in your www folder (2 files, jquery.gridster.min.js and jquery.gridster.min.css).  You will also need to add "custom.js" into the www folder, which I have also provided below. 

Also, I found the shinyGridster library, but even when I switch to that I got the exact same behaviour.  I think it must be something about how renderUI() creates the HTML and for some reason the JavaScript can't see it. 


**** www/custom.js ****
$(document).ready(function(){
    $(".gridster ul").gridster({
        widget_margins: [10, 10],
        widget_base_dimensions: [140, 140]
    });
});


**** app.R ****
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)

ui <- fluidPage(
 
  tags$head(
    # JQuery JS
    tags$script(src="https://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.12.0/jquery.min.js"),
    # Gridster JS
    tags$script(src="jquery.gridster.min.js"),
    # Gridster CSS
    tags$link(href = "jquery.gridster.min.css", rel = "stylesheet"),
    # custom CSS to initialize Gridster in document.ready()
    tags$script(src="custom.js")  
  ),

  fluidRow(width=12,
    column(12,
           
      # dynamic version - doesn't work
      uiOutput("dynamicStuff"),
     
      # hand coded version - works!
      tags$div(class="gridster",
        tags$ul(
          tags$li("data-row" = 1, "data-col" = "1", "data-sizex" = "1", "data-sizey" = "1",
            p("Placeholder.. Hand coded... normally I have lots of various plots, etc. here...")
          ),
          tags$li("data-row" = 2, "data-col" = "1", "data-sizex" = "1", "data-sizey" = "1",
            p("Another Hand coded placeholder.. ")
           )
        ) #end tags$ul
      ) #end div class=gridster
     
     
    ) #end column
  ) #end fluidRow
) #end fluidPage                                  

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # simplified data set... in my App, iris is replaced with a dataframe that has lots of processing as it is constantly changing
  myData <- reactive({
    iris
  })
 
  # Dynamically generate UI stuff - based on https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/xW8f5g5gm4s
  output$dynamicStuff <- renderUI({
   
    # vector to hold each individual <li> element.  I don't know if I actually need a vector, I was just following the example.
    #  I only seemed to need 1 slot
    list_of_LIs <- vector("list", 1)
   
    # count the number of <li/>s needed based on the dataframe
    number_of_LIs <- nrow(myData()  %>% group_by(Species)  %>% count(Species))
   
    # Loop to create UI stuff for each object  (ex. in iris, this loops through setosa, versicolor, virginica)
    for(i in 1:number_of_LIs) {
     
      list_of_LIs[[i]] <-  list(
       
        # Make a <li/> element for each draggable fruit/veg panel for Gridster
        tags$li("data-row" = i, "data-col" = "1", "data-sizex" = "1", "data-sizey" = "1",
         
          # for simplicity, replace various plots etc. with a simple placeholder
          p(paste0("Dynamically generated row number ", i))
         
        )
      ) #end list
    } #end for
   
    # Assemble  <li/> elements inside <div class="gridster"><ul> HERE </ul></div>
    return(
      tags$div(class="gridster",
               tags$ul(
                 #list of li's - convert to a tagList because https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/
                 do.call(tagList, list_of_LIs)
               ) #end ul
      ) #end div class=gridster
    ) #end return
  }) #end renderUI
 
} #end server function

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: problem with renderUI() and JavaScript
parts:
Hi,

I found a previous post that helped me make progress on this:  https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/8rYYHhoM0pg

In custom.js, I added the following. 
$(document).on("click", "#dynamicStuff", function(e){

$(".gridster ul").gridster({
        widget_margins: [10, 10],
        widget_base_dimensions: [140, 140]
    });
});

After the HTML is done being created by renderUI(), the user needs to click somewhere on the dynamic content, then the dragging functionality appears.  yay!  Unfortunately, it is annoying to force the user to click somewhere before the dragging functionality becomes available.  There's probably a way to make this happen automatically and I'll update this thread if I ever find it.  But, this is my problem with JavaScript and is not an R/Shiny problem. 

Thanks! bye,
SF

messages.subject: Re: problem with renderUI() and JavaScript
parts:
(The do.call(tagList, ...) shouldn't be required, btw. I'm not exactly sure why Winston's code has that either but I'm pretty sure your situation doesn't require it)

If it's ok to call the gridster method multiple times on an li, then the div you return in your renderUI can contain a tags$script('$(".gridster li").gridster(...etc...);') as an additional element.

    number_of_LIs <- nrow(myData()  %>% group_by(Species)  %>% count(Species))
   
    # Loop to create UI stuff for each object  (ex. in iris, this loops through setosa, versicolor, virginica)
    for(i in 1:number_of_LIs) {
     
      list_of_LIs[[i]] <-  list(
       
        # Make a <li/> element for each draggable fruit/veg panel for Gridster
        tags$li("data-row" = i, "data-col" = "1", "data-sizex" = "1", "data-sizey" = "1",
         
          # for simplicity, replace various plots etc. with a simple placeholder
          p(paste0("Dynamically generated row number ", i))
         
        )
      ) #end list
    } #end for
   
    # Assemble  <li/> elements inside <div class="gridster"><ul> HERE </ul></div>
    return(
      tags$div(class="gridster",
               tags$ul(
                 #list of li's - convert to a tagList because https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415/
                 do.call(tagList, list_of_LIs)
               ) #end ul
      ) #end div class=gridster
    ) #end return
  }) #end renderUI
 
} #end server function

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
